part_title: Managed AI APIs and Amazon Comprehend Text Analysis
review_basis: Narrations prepared against current lesson-map notes and service lifecycle caveats; original images and slide counts audited at rendering preflight. Direct visual inspection of slide image layouts was not available in this session.

scenes.title: Why AWS AI Managed Services?
scenes.narration: Begin with a common business request: extracting useful information without building and hosting a machine learning model from scratch. A managed service exposes an API that accepts a supported input and returns an output. Different services solve different tasks, so a text analysis API is not interchangeable with image recognition or speech generation. AWS handles parts of the infrastructure, but the customer remains responsible for using the API correctly, configuring security, validating outputs, and controlling costs. Compare region availability, quotas, synchronous versus batch modes, data handling and per-request or per-unit pricing. Some services charge for characters, images, pages or audio duration rather than model tokens. The exam decision is to identify the business input and required output before choosing a named service.

scenes.title: Amazon Comprehend
scenes.narration: Imagine a support team collecting feedback about a product. Amazon Comprehend can identify sentiment and extract entities or key phrases from supported text. A statement like I love the camera but delivery was late can contain mixed evidence, so one overall sentiment score should not be treated as a definitive understanding of the customer's intention. Check feature-specific language and batch support. When the task instead requires finding current policy facts, retrieval may be a better tool than sentiment analysis. Some historical Comprehend capabilities named in older courses are no longer open to new customers; check feature eligibility before planning a new deployment. An exam question asking for entity names or sentiment from ordinary language is different from one asking a chatbot to compose new paragraphs.

scenes.title: Comprehend – Custom Classification
scenes.narration: Custom classification teaches a model to assign a document to a business-defined category. For example, a complaint about an unexpected charge may need the Billing label, while a broken package belongs to Delivery. A team prepares correctly labeled examples, keeps evaluation examples separate, trains the classifier and measures how often new documents are categorized correctly. Classification typically produces a category for the document or supplied input. It does not highlight every specific phrase that names a product. Input formats and synchronous or batch invocation differ by feature and model configuration. If the model confuses categories, inspect the training examples and the class balance before trusting a confidence score. Check whether the task asks for the document's overall category or individual entities embedded inside it.

scenes.title: Named Entity Recognition (NER)
scenes.narration: Named entity recognition locates spans of text and assigns entity types. In the sample sentence Ravi visits Pune on Friday, a recognizer may mark Ravi as a person, Pune as a location and Friday as a date or temporal expression. Notice that the result points to text spans, not just a single label for the whole sentence. Detecting a person's name is not equivalent to identifying the person uniquely. A common name can refer to many individuals, and the model has no proof of identity merely because it found the name. Entities may also be quantities, organizations, events or other supported types. For verification, review the surrounding sentence, the extracted boundaries and whether the chosen type actually fits. Compare this with classification: classification labels a message; NER labels mentions inside that message.

scenes.title: Comprehend – Custom Entity Recognition
scenes.narration: Custom entity recognition is useful when a company needs domain-specific names that a generic model might not recognize. Imagine extracting its own device model numbers or internal contract codes from customer emails. Annotators mark examples of the exact spans and agree on consistent label definitions. The training set must represent variations, spelling mistakes and surrounding contexts, while separate test material checks unseen documents. Precision asks how many extracted items were truly the desired type; recall asks how many of the actual desired mentions were found. A high value for one does not guarantee the other. Do not confuse extracting an order identifier from text with categorizing the entire ticket as a refund request. Choose custom entity recognition for spans, and custom classification for document-level labels.
